title: Four A.M. Proof
subject: the overnight baker at a supermarket in-store bakery waiting on dough to prove at four in the morning while the shelf-stackers argue about football
caption: Grunge revival in the 2025 Los Angeles young-band style, loud-quiet-loud. Clean arpeggiated electric guitar in the verses; heavy fuzz drop-D guitars slamming in for the chorus; a distorted bass doubling the riff; pounding live drums with washing crash cymbals. Thick, garage-loud production, wide guitars, vocal slightly buried in the mix. Male baritone, slurred and low in the verses, rising to a hoarse shouted chorus. 118 BPM, D minor. Bleary, sardonic and restless. No nu-metal rap, no screamed metalcore breakdown, no autotune, no electronic drums, no pop-punk brightness.
lyrics:
[Intro - detuned guitar and bass, slow]

[Verse 1]
Hairnet, white clogs, the oven clock says four
Two hundred baguettes and nobody wants more
The dough's in the cabinet, it's taking its time
Somebody's stacking beans in aisle nine

[Pre-Chorus]
Can't rush it, can't rush it
It rises when it wants

[Chorus]
Proof, proof, come up for me
I've been awake since yesterday
Proof, proof, the doors open at eight
And I'm the one they'll blame

[Verse 2]
Flour in my eyebrows, flour in my phone
The radio plays one song and leaves me alone
Gary's on the forklift telling everyone
Who should've played striker, who should've run

[Pre-Chorus]
Can't rush it, can't rush it
It's doubled, nearly done

[Chorus]
Proof, proof, come up for me
Slash the tops and in they go
Proof, proof, the doors open at eight
And nobody will know

[Outro - feedback and a slow tom]
Smells like a morning
I'm going home to bed
